questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find mushrooms in the forest
Whether medicinal mushrooms really work
Which mushrooms are poisonous
Animals with strange names that live in zoos
questions.why: Beth asks how real the supposed health benefits of mushrooms are.

questions.q: What does Neil first think “Lion's Mane” and “Turkey Tail” are?
options: Things you might find in a zoo
Types of medicine
Names of new restaurants in London
Kinds of flowers
questions.why: He says they sound like things you might find in the zoo.

questions.q: How much was the global medicinal mushroom market worth in 2021?
options: 2.6 million dollars
260 billion dollars
26 billion dollars
6 billion dollars
questions.why: Neil says it was valued at 26 billion dollars and growing.

questions.q: According to Dr Emily Leeming, what kind of benefits are mushroom labels mostly claiming?
options: Better skin and shinier, stronger hair
Stronger bones
Weight loss
Mental benefits, like less anxiety
questions.why: She says they're labelled “super brain drugs” for lessening anxiety and depression.

questions.q: What does Dr Leeming think about these claims?
options: They are proven by many studies
They are true, but only for young people who try them
They are dangerous lies
They seem exaggerated, with little evidence in humans
questions.why: She says they seem quite overblown and the evidence on humans is very limited.

questions.q: Why does Beth mention chamomile tea?
options: To recommend it instead of mushrooms
To show it is made from mushrooms
To show that helpful things aren't always legal medicines
To say that chamomile tea has now been banned in some countries
questions.why: It may help you relax, but without scientific proof you can't legally call it a medicine.

questions.q: What does Emma Clifford say about consumers?
options: They only trust modern science
Many want proof, but ancient wisdom also persuades them
They have stopped buying mushrooms
They don't really care about health claims on food at all
questions.why: She says ancient wisdom may be just as compelling, if not more so, than modern science.

questions.q: How do young people feel about medicinal mushrooms, according to Emma Clifford?
options: Curious and keen to try them
Afraid of them
Bored by them
Angry about their high prices in shops
questions.why: She says young people in particular are really intrigued to give these ingredients a go.
